image.alt: A young fiddle-leaf fig with large glossy green violin-shaped leaves, in a white pot

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates gentle direct sun once it is used to it

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; shelter it from strong wind and harsh afternoon sun

home_use.note: Choose a spot and leave it; it dislikes being moved

snap: A bold indoor tree with large, glossy, violin-shaped leaves and a sculptural shape. It rewards a bright spot and a steady routine, but it sulks if you move it or overwater it. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed, and the milky sap irritates skin.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Native to the lowland rainforests of tropical West Africa, where it can grow into a tree 12 m tall or more, often starting life high in another tree. Indoors it grows slowly into a tree 1.5–2 m tall, with the big, leathery, veined leaves held on a single upright stem.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Pick a bright spot with indirect light and leave it there. This plant hates being moved, drafts and sudden changes, and it drops leaves when stressed. Water when the top 3–5 cm of soil is dry, usually about once a week, and never let it sit in water. Turn the pot a quarter turn now and then so it grows evenly.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The huge, violin-shaped leaves make it a living sculpture, and it works as the single statement plant of a room. Each new leaf unfurls from a pointed bud sheath that later drops off. Wipe the leaves with a damp cloth to keep them glossy and to help them take up light. It can be pruned to shape or to keep it compact.
